title: I'm not letting Claude touch my passwords, no matter how safe Anthropic claims it is
content_html:
Published Jul 25, 2026, 1:00 PM EDT

Irene Okpanachi is a Features writer covering Android devices, laptops, portable projectors, VR headsets, software, and AI recorders for Android Police and Talk Android.

She has five years' experience across the Tech, E-commerce, and Food niches, with over 1,000 posts published. The Tech space is where she geeks out most, particularly Android.

Irene holds certifications in Graphic Design (HerTechTrail), Writing in Plain Language (LinkedIn), and English for IT (Cisco Networking Academy).

Beyond writing, Irene is a gamer, singer/songwriter, food lover, and a Jack of all trades.

I've accepted that artificial intelligence is the future. What concerns me is how companies are turning my vulnerability into a product.

It makes me nostalgic for a time when advice around security methods was much simpler.

After the Conficker worm infected millions of computers in 2009, schools, governments, and even parents warned against sharing passwords.

So, allowing artificial intelligence to sign in to my accounts wasn't on my 2026 bingo card. Here's why it scares me.

I don't want AI browsing the web on my behalf

It doesn't need access to my accounts

Anthropic and 1Password recently announced a zero-exposure integration system. It lets Claude log in to your accounts on your behalf without reading the password string.

I didn't even know the tool could order my groceries until I started researching the capability.

I recently switched from my ChatGPT Go subscription to Claude Pro. The plan made the capability accessible through the Claude in Chrome extension.

The AI can navigate websites, compare deals, add items to a cart, and update account details.

But the process ends when it hits an authentication wall. After that, you'll log in yourself and complete transactions.

1Password for Claude supposedly removes this bottleneck. It identifies the credential Claude needs to use and requests your biometric approval.

Then it fills in the login form without leaking password characters or the one-time code. It must request permission again before using the same credential next time.

Unfortunately, zero-exposure is as much a marketing term as it is a security one. You're basically blindfolding one part of the process.

It only applies to the password string itself. Claude still receives an active session for the duration of the task and can act within your account with the same permissions you have.

A recent AI security incident reinforced my concerns

It was no little coincidence

I was in the middle of drafting this piece when a notification popped up on my screen.

Hugging Face had announced a security incident, and OpenAI later confirmed its models were responsible. I paused to acknowledge my goosebumps before I continued reading.

OpenAI's models were operating in a restricted test environment with limited network access. They exploited an unknown vulnerability to escape the sandbox and hack into Hugging Face's servers to find the answers on their own.

The timing couldn't have been more ironic. I don't always respond to every bad AI announcement.

I've spent the past few years using ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and more obscure models. They've helped me research and organize ideas. But I also pay attention to the data.

Although OpenAI's model wasn't acting with malicious intent, it reminded me that AI is optimized for goals and cannot use common sense. Give it an objective, and it may find multiple ways to reach it.

Some of those paths may cross boundaries you flag as inappropriate. I'm worried AI agents have increasing privileges and access when even the companies building them admit to their flaws.

Prompt injection remains an unsolved problem.

Anthropic's own testing found its browser agent could be hijacked 32% of the time before any safeguards.

So, security is among the few areas I prefer to keep AI at arm's length. My caution around it didn't appear overnight. It took me years to accept password managers in the first place.

I already know what a compromised session costs

My perspective changed after an account takeover

Password managers offer the convenience of storing every password in one encrypted vault. I eventually stopped thinking about logins altogether.

Earlier this year, my confidence was shaken when I started receiving random two-factor authentication codes from Ubisoft, PlayStation, and Electronic Arts.

I assumed they were phishing attempts until someone changed the email address on my EA account.

It hit me how close I came to losing a decade of game progress, cloud saves, digital purchases, and linked payment methods.

The next 48 hours became a recovery exercise I don't want to repeat. I came away from it with a different perspective.

Even though password managers are more secure than reusing passwords or relying on memory, they require me to trust another company with one of the most sensitive parts of my digital life. They can still be breached.

It had already happened to LastPass in 2022 when attackers walked away with encrypted vaults belonging to millions of users.

They used a compromised developer machine, which gave them access to the cloud storage environment where encrypted vaults were backed up.

Even though the encryption worked, the vaults were in someone else's hands. You were exposed to an offline cracking attempt if you had a weak master password.

I retained my confidence in password managers

Just not on everything

I've used Google Password Manager for years, but I've become increasingly uncomfortable with Google's broader approach to data collection.

In 2025, it was caught expanding collected data through Chrome's Privacy Sandbox. The excuse was that it was targeted tracking as a privacy feature, but the underlying data collection continued.

Although my security-conscious friends vouch for password managers, I remained unconvinced.

So, I shared my most critical passwords across my 1Password, my physical journal, and hard drives.

I switched to 1Password because of its dual-key model. It encrypts my vault with a master password and a secret key that never leaves my device.

So, even a compromised Google account can't affect it. I change my primary email and financial account passwords every three months. Gaming, social media, and work accounts change every six months.

Everything else changes once a year, or immediately after any platform announces a breach.

Manually saved passwords are not safe. They can't automatically monitor for breaches and alert me when my credentials leak.

But they're no longer stored in a remotely accessible password vault, which is the risk I'm trying to avoid.

I've also enabled app-based two-factor authentication to strengthen my accounts, and use passkeys where necessary.

Convenience has a cost

As I move more of my digital life toward self-hosting, I'm trying to reduce dependencies. Cloud storage, email servers, streaming licenses, and app ecosystems are among them.

So, I don't see AI browsing for me all the way down to an order. It doesn't feel like the time saved is worth introducing another layer of trust.

But if convenience is your priority, and you have faith in the company's architecture, use features like 1Password for Claude with caution.

Check your active sessions regularly on any account the AI touches.

sentences.zh: 我以不同的视角摆脱了它。

blocks.html_en: Even though password managers are more secure than reusing passwords or relying on memory, they require me to trust another company with one of the most sensitive parts of my digital life. They can still be breached.

sentences.en: Even though password managers are more secure than reusing passwords or relying on memory, they require me to trust another company with one of the most sensitive parts of my digital life.
sentences.zh: 尽管密码管理器比重复使用密码或依赖记忆更安全，但它们要求我信任另一家拥有我数字生活中最敏感部分的公司。

sentences.en: They can still be breached.
sentences.zh: 它们仍然可能被破坏。

blocks.html_en: It had already happened to LastPass in 2022 when attackers walked away with encrypted vaults belonging to millions of users.

sentences.en: It had already happened to LastPass in 2022 when attackers walked away with encrypted vaults belonging to millions of users.
sentences.zh: 2022 年 LastPass 就曾发生过这样的情况，攻击者带走了数百万用户的加密保管库。

blocks.html_en: They used a compromised developer machine, which gave them access to the cloud storage environment where encrypted vaults were backed up.

sentences.en: They used a compromised developer machine, which gave them access to the cloud storage environment where encrypted vaults were backed up.
sentences.zh: 他们使用了受感染的开发人员机器，这使他们能够访问备份加密保管库的云存储环境。

blocks.html_en: Even though the encryption worked, the vaults were in someone else's hands. You were exposed to an offline cracking attempt if you had a weak master password.

sentences.en: Even though the encryption worked, the vaults were in someone else's hands.
sentences.zh: 尽管加密有效，但金库仍在其他人手中。

sentences.en: You were exposed to an offline cracking attempt if you had a weak master password.
sentences.zh: 如果您的主密码较弱，您就会面临离线破解尝试。

blocks.html_en: I retained my confidence in password managers

sentences.en: I retained my confidence in password managers
sentences.zh: 我对密码管理器保持信心

blocks.html_en: Just not on everything

sentences.en: Just not on everything
sentences.zh: 只是不是在所有事情上

blocks.html_en: I've used Google Password Manager for years, but I've become increasingly uncomfortable with Google's broader approach to data collection.

sentences.en: I've used Google Password Manager for years, but I've become increasingly uncomfortable with Google's broader approach to data collection.
sentences.zh: 我已经使用 Google 密码管理器多年，但我对 Google 更广泛的数据收集方法越来越感到不舒服。

blocks.html_en: In 2025, it was caught expanding collected data through Chrome's Privacy Sandbox. The excuse was that it was targeted tracking as a privacy feature, but the underlying data collection continued.

sentences.en: In 2025, it was caught expanding collected data through Chrome's Privacy Sandbox.
sentences.zh: 2025 年，它被发现通过 Chrome 的隐私沙箱扩展收集的数据。

sentences.en: The excuse was that it was targeted tracking as a privacy feature, but the underlying data collection continued.
sentences.zh: 借口是它是作为隐私功能进行有针对性的跟踪，但底层数据收集仍在继续。

blocks.html_en: Although my security-conscious friends vouch for password managers, I remained unconvinced.

sentences.en: Although my security-conscious friends vouch for password managers, I remained unconvinced.
sentences.zh: 尽管我的具有安全意识的朋友们都为密码管理器提供担保，但我仍然不相信。

blocks.html_en: So, I shared my most critical passwords across my 1Password, my physical journal, and hard drives.

sentences.en: So, I shared my most critical passwords across my 1Password, my physical journal, and hard drives.
sentences.zh: 因此，我在 1Password、物理日记和硬盘上共享了最重要的密码。

blocks.html_en: I switched to 1Password because of its dual-key model. It encrypts my vault with a master password and a secret key that never leaves my device.

sentences.en: I switched to 1Password because of its dual-key model.
sentences.zh: 我改用 1Password 因为它的双密钥模型。

sentences.en: It encrypts my vault with a master password and a secret key that never leaves my device.
sentences.zh: 它使用主密码和永远不会离开我的设备的密钥对我的保管库进行加密。

blocks.html_en: So, even a compromised Google account can't affect it. I change my primary email and financial account passwords every three months. Gaming, social media, and work accounts change every six months.

sentences.en: So, even a compromised Google account can't affect it.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使 Google 帐户遭到入侵也不会对其产生影响。

sentences.en: I change my primary email and financial account passwords every three months.
sentences.zh: 我每三个月更改一次主要电子邮件和财务帐户密码。

sentences.en: Gaming, social media, and work accounts change every six months.
sentences.zh: 游戏、社交媒体和工作帐户每六个月更改一次。

blocks.html_en: Everything else changes once a year, or immediately after any platform announces a breach.

sentences.en: Everything else changes once a year, or immediately after any platform announces a breach.
sentences.zh: 其他所有内容每年都会更改一次，或者在任何平台宣布违规后立即更改。

blocks.html_en: Manually saved passwords are not safe. They can't automatically monitor for breaches and alert me when my credentials leak.

sentences.en: Manually saved passwords are not safe.
sentences.zh: 手动保存的密码并不安全。

sentences.en: They can't automatically monitor for breaches and alert me when my credentials leak.
sentences.zh: 他们无法自动监控违规行为并在我的凭据泄露时提醒我。

blocks.html_en: But they're no longer stored in a remotely accessible password vault, which is the risk I'm trying to avoid.

sentences.en: But they're no longer stored in a remotely accessible password vault, which is the risk I'm trying to avoid.
sentences.zh: 但它们不再存储在可远程访问的密码库中，这是我试图避免的风险。

blocks.html_en: I've also enabled app-based two-factor authentication to strengthen my accounts, and use passkeys where necessary.

sentences.en: I've also enabled app-based two-factor authentication to strengthen my accounts, and use passkeys where necessary.
sentences.zh: 我还启用了基于应用程序的双因素身份验证来增强我的帐户，并在必要时使用密钥。

blocks.html_en: Convenience has a cost

sentences.en: Convenience has a cost
sentences.zh: 便利是有代价的

blocks.html_en: As I move more of my digital life toward self-hosting, I'm trying to reduce dependencies. Cloud storage, email servers, streaming licenses, and app ecosystems are among them.

sentences.en: As I move more of my digital life toward self-hosting, I'm trying to reduce dependencies.
sentences.zh: 当我将更多的数字生活转向自托管时，我正在努力减少依赖性。

sentences.en: Cloud storage, email servers, streaming licenses, and app ecosystems are among them.
sentences.zh: 云存储、电子邮件服务器、流媒体许可证和应用程序生态系统都在其中。

blocks.html_en: So, I don't see AI browsing for me all the way down to an order. It doesn't feel like the time saved is worth introducing another layer of trust.

sentences.en: So, I don't see AI browsing for me all the way down to an order.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不认为人工智能会为我浏览整个订单。

sentences.en: It doesn't feel like the time saved is worth introducing another layer of trust.
sentences.zh: 感觉节省的时间不值得引入另一层信任。

blocks.html_en: But if convenience is your priority, and you have faith in the company's architecture, use features like 1Password for Claude with caution.

sentences.en: But if convenience is your priority, and you have faith in the company's architecture, use features like 1Password for Claude with caution.
sentences.zh: 但如果方便是您的首要任务，并且您对公司的架构有信心，请谨慎使用 1Password for Claude 等功能。

blocks.html_en: Check your active sessions regularly on any account the AI touches.

sentences.en: Check your active sessions regularly on any account the AI touches.
sentences.zh: 定期检查人工智能接触的任何帐户的活动会话。

content_html_zh:
发布于 2026 年 7 月 25 日下午 1:00（美国东部时间）

Irene Okpanachi 是一位专题作家，涵盖 Android 设备、笔记本电脑、便携式投影仪、VR 耳机、软件以及适用于 Android Police 和 Talk Android 的 AI 录音机。

她在科技、电子商务和食品领域拥有 5 年经验，发表了 1,000 多篇帖子。 科技领域是她最感兴趣的领域，尤其是 Android。

Irene 拥有平面设计 (HerTechTrail)、平白语言写作 (LinkedIn) 和 IT 英语 (思科网络学院) 认证。

除了写作之外，艾琳还是一名游戏玩家、歌手/词曲作者、美食爱好者和多才多艺。

我已经接受人工智能是未来。 我担心的是公司如何将我的弱点变成产品。

这让我怀念那个关于安全方法的建议要简单得多的时代。

2009 年 Conficker 蠕虫病毒感染了数百万台计算机后，学校、政府甚至家长都警告不要共享密码。

因此，允许人工智能登录我的帐户并不在我的 2026 年宾果卡上。 这就是为什么它让我害怕。

我不希望人工智能代表我浏览网页

它不需要访问我的帐户

Anthropic 和 1Password 最近宣布推出零暴露集成系统。 它可以让 Claude 代表您登录您的帐户，而无需读取密码字符串。

在我开始研究该功能之前，我什至不知道该工具可以订购我的杂货。

我最近从 ChatGPT Go 订阅切换到 Claude Pro。 该计划使该功能可以通过 Chrome 扩展中的 Claude 访问。

人工智能可以导航网站、比较交易、将商品添加到购物车以及更新帐户详细信息。

但当遇到身份验证墙时，该过程就会结束。 之后，您将自行登录并完成交易。

1Password for Claude 据说可以消除这个瓶颈。 它识别克劳德需要使用的凭据并请求您的生物识别批准。

然后它会填写登录表单，而不会泄露密码字符或一次性代码。 在下次使用相同的凭据之前，它必须再次请求许可。

不幸的是，零暴露既是一个营销术语，也是一个安全术语。 你基本上是蒙住了整个过程的一部分。

它仅适用于密码字符串本身。 在任务期间，Claude 仍然会收到一个活动会话，并且可以使用您拥有的相同权限在您的帐户中进行操作。

最近的一次人工智能安全事件加深了我的担忧

这并非小巧合

当我正在起草这篇文章时，屏幕上弹出了一条通知。

Hugging Face 宣布发生安全事件，OpenAI 随后确认其模型对此负责。 在继续阅读之前，我停下来承认我的鸡皮疙瘩。

OpenAI 的模型在网络访问受限的受限测试环境中运行。 他们利用一个未知的漏洞逃离沙箱，并侵入 Hugging Face 的服务器，自行寻找答案。

这个时机再讽刺不过了。 我并不总是对每一个糟糕的人工智能公告做出回应。

在过去的几年里，我一直在使用 ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini 和其他一些不起眼的模型。 他们帮助我研究和组织想法。 但我也关注数据。

虽然 OpenAI 的模型并没有恶意，但它提醒我，AI 是针对目标进行优化的，不能使用常识。 给它一个目标，它可能会找到多种方法来实现它。

其中一些路径可能会跨越您标记为不适当的边界。 我担心人工智能代理拥有越来越多的特权和访问权限，即使是构建它们的公司也承认它们的缺陷。

及时注射仍然是一个未解决的问题。

Anthropic 自己的测试发现，在采取任何防护措施之前，其浏览器代理有 32% 的可能性会被劫持。

因此，安全是我更愿意与人工智能保持距离的少数几个领域之一。 我对它的谨慎并不是一夜之间出现的。 我花了很多年才接受密码管理器。

我已经知道受损会话的成本

帐户被接管后我的观点发生了变化

密码管理器提供了将每个密码存储在一个加密保管库中的便利。 我最终完全不再考虑登录。

今年早些时候，当我开始收到来自育碧、PlayStation 和艺电的随机双因素验证码时，我的信心动摇了。

我以为他们是网络钓鱼尝试，直到有人更改了我 EA 帐户上的电子邮件地址。

我突然意识到，我差点就失去了十年来的游戏进度、云保存、数字购买和链接支付方式。

接下来的 48 小时变成了我不想重复的恢复练习。 我以不同的视角摆脱了它。

尽管密码管理器比重复使用密码或依赖记忆更安全，但它们要求我信任另一家拥有我数字生活中最敏感部分的公司。 它们仍然可能被破坏。

2022 年 LastPass 就曾发生过这样的情况，攻击者带走了数百万用户的加密保管库。

他们使用了受感染的开发人员机器，这使他们能够访问备份加密保管库的云存储环境。

尽管加密有效，但金库仍在其他人手中。 如果您的主密码较弱，您就会面临离线破解尝试。

我对密码管理器保持信心

只是不是在所有事情上

我已经使用 Google 密码管理器多年，但我对 Google 更广泛的数据收集方法越来越感到不舒服。

2025 年，它被发现通过 Chrome 的隐私沙箱扩展收集的数据。 借口是它是作为隐私功能进行有针对性的跟踪，但底层数据收集仍在继续。

尽管我的具有安全意识的朋友们都为密码管理器提供担保，但我仍然不相信。

因此，我在 1Password、物理日记和硬盘上共享了最重要的密码。

我改用 1Password 因为它的双密钥模型。 它使用主密码和永远不会离开我的设备的密钥对我的保管库进行加密。

因此，即使 Google 帐户遭到入侵也不会对其产生影响。 我每三个月更改一次主要电子邮件和财务帐户密码。 游戏、社交媒体和工作帐户每六个月更改一次。

其他所有内容每年都会更改一次，或者在任何平台宣布违规后立即更改。

手动保存的密码并不安全。 他们无法自动监控违规行为并在我的凭据泄露时提醒我。

但它们不再存储在可远程访问的密码库中，这是我试图避免的风险。

我还启用了基于应用程序的双因素身份验证来增强我的帐户，并在必要时使用密钥。

便利是有代价的

当我将更多的数字生活转向自托管时，我正在努力减少依赖性。 云存储、电子邮件服务器、流媒体许可证和应用程序生态系统都在其中。

所以，我不认为人工智能会为我浏览整个订单。 感觉节省的时间不值得引入另一层信任。

但如果方便是您的首要任务，并且您对公司的架构有信心，请谨慎使用 1Password for Claude 等功能。

定期检查人工智能接触的任何帐户的活动会话。
